newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU condemns executions in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: EU condemns executions in Burundi.

text.p: The European Union condemned on Wednesday Burundi's execution of six prisoners accused of genocide, saying it cast doubt on the country's commitment to peace negotiations that will begin later this month.
"The executions...send out negative signals both to the partners in the negotiations and to the international community," the EU said in a statement issued by Luxembourg, its current president.
The EU said the prisoners, accused of playing a leading role in 1993 inter-ethnic massacres, did not receive a fair trial before their July 31 hangings.
"The EU notes with concern that the execution of the six prisoners bears all the hallmarks of a deliberate political act," the statement said.
The United States, Zimbabwe, Tanzania and Amnesty International have also criticised the executions.
More than 150,000 people have died in Burundi since October 1993, when the country's first freely elected Hutu president, Melchior Ndadaye, was murdered by Tutsi troops in an attempted coup.

The coup attempt was followed by a wave of reprisals by enraged Hutus, widely regarded as "genocide" by Burundi's Tutsi minority, and counter-reprisals by the Tutsi-dominated army. All-party peace talks are scheduled to begin on August 25 in Arusha, Tanzania -- the first between the government of military leader Pierre Buyoya and the main Hutu rebel group, the National Council for the Defence of Democracy.

"While recognising that the cycle of impunity in Burundi must be broken, the EU considers that legal certainty in Burundi can only be reestablished by means of trials which offer all the judicial safeguards of the rule of law," the EU said.
